subject: EU/UK transfer route decision — SCCs & UK addendum (Galenix request)
messages:
From: Elena Mitrov <elena.mitrov@glnx.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Simon Price <simon.price@hendersonlaw.com>
Date: 2026-11-24T09:12:00Z
Subject: Data transfer route for Redwood services (Galenix)

Hi Alex,

Quick one from our side as we prepare to onboard Redwood for processing patient scheduling data: our DPO is asking that you confirm which EU->UK transfer mechanism you intend to use and the proposed SCC module(s). We have to list the route in our DPIA and procurement checklist by next Friday.

Specifically can you confirm: 
- Whether Redwood will rely on the EU Commission Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) or an alternative (e.g., UK Addendum, adequacy + contract mix).
- Which SCC module(s) you propose (Controller-controller, Controller-processor, Processor-processor) and any intended addendum.
- Any evidence we can attach (execution checklist or signing timeline).

We appreciate a short note and an optional exec timeline — our legal team will review.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Mitrov
Data Protection Officer
Galenix Health

Attachments: procurement_requirements_Galenix.pdf (attached by Galenix)

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Mitrov <elena.mitrov@glnx.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-24T14:38:00Z
Subject: Re: Data transfer route for Redwood services (Galenix)

Elena — thanks for the clear ask. High level answer below; legal (Rishi) and compliance (Monica) are looped in for details and evidence.

Summary recommendation (short):
- Primary route: Execute the EU Commission SCCs with the UK Addendum (dual-signature approach). For processor operations the practical pattern will be: Module 2 (processor -> processor) where applicable; Module 1 if we end up in controller-controller relationships for specific features (rare).
- Fallback: If Galenix prefers controller-controlled allocation for certain exports, we can offer a hybrid (Module 1 + specific statements).
- Evidence: attaching an internal comparison spreadsheet and an execution checklist showing required signatories and timeline.

Why this route: the EU SCCs + UK Addendum covers both EU->EEA and EU->UK movements without relying on narrow derogations, and it aligns with our standard private deployment legal posture. It also keeps continuity for customers who run mixed-region setups.

Next steps I propose:
1) Laura / Rishi: confirm whether we need to update our data flow annex to call out Galenix-specific subprocessors.
2) Monica: prepare the execution checklist + evidence bundle for Galenix (SOC 2 references, KMS notes).
3) I will send a final confirmation to Elena and share a DocuSign envelope for the SCCs + UK Addendum by 2026-12-02, target signature by 2026-12-09.

Attachments: scc-module-matrix-20261124.xlsx

Best,
Alex Martinez
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T10:40:00Z

Alex / team, quick thoughts: 
- I agree with EU SCCs + UK Addendum as the primary execution path. However, we should be explicit in the Annex about who is Controller vs Processor for each data flow (scheduling / analytics / anonymized logs). That will determine whether Module 1 or Module 2 applies on a per-feature basis.
- Proposed language: include a short "role matrix" in the DPA annex and a list of named subprocessors for Galenix (or a commitment to provide within 30 days of go-live).
- Evidence: I'll prepare a redlined SCCs package and a short cover memo explaining the module choice rationale for Galenix legal. Simon (Henderson) should review the memo.

Monica, please prepare the SOC 2 excerpts and the runtime encryption notes.

Rishi

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-30T16:20:00Z
Subject: Final confirmation: EU SCCs + UK Addendum; execution plan (Galenix)

Elena — following internal review, final confirmation and execution plan below. Thanks for the patience.

What we'll sign: EU Commission Standard Contractual Clauses (most recent template) paired with the Redwood UK Addendum to cover transfers to the UK.

Module approach (practical):
- Processor relationships (Redwood processing on Galenix's behalf): Module 2 will apply to the data flows associated with scheduling APIs, real-time tokenized logs, and telemetry.
- Controller-controller / hybrid features: we will call out any specific features that operate under Module 1 in the Annex.

Required evidence bundle (attached):
- redwood-sccs-exec-checklist-20261130.pdf (who signs, timeline, signatory blocks)
- SOC 2 excerpts (SOC-2-Type-2-summary.pdf referenced in the bundle)
- scc-module-matrix-20261124.xlsx (mapping of features to modules)

Timeline:
- 2026-12-02: DocuSign envelope sent (SCCs + UK Addendum).
- 2026-12-09: Target signatures completed.
- Post-signature: we will deliver a named-subprocessor list or a 30-day commitment to provide one.

Simon — appreciate a quick review of the memo/annex we will send with the DocuSign envelope.

If this works for Galenix, please confirm and we'll proceed to send the envelope.

Best regards,
Alex Martinez
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com
